diagnostic_reports.conclusion: Day 5 post laparoscopic appendectomy. Port sites healing well, no signs of wound infection or dehiscence. Abdomen soft and non-tender on palpation. Bowel sounds present. Patient tolerating oral fluids and light diet. No surgical complications identified. Surgical team satisfied with recovery trajectory.

NOTED ANOMALY: Haemoglobin 9.8 g/dL — mild anaemia secondary to operative blood loss compounded by pre-existing iron deficiency. Ferritin critically low at 11 ng/mL. However, haemoglobin is stable and trending upward (was 8.4 on Day 1). Oral ferrous sulfate initiated. Transfusion threshold not met. Safe to continue oral iron as outpatient. Follow-up FBC in 4 weeks.

NOTED ANOMALY: HbA1c 8.1% and fasting glucose 152 mg/dL indicate suboptimal glycaemic control. However, values are stable and not acutely dangerous. Elevated glucose is partly attributable to surgical stress response. Patient is established on Metformin. Outpatient diabetology appointment booked within 2 weeks to review and optimise regimen. Not a barrier to discharge.
